title: Nino 3.4 gave no clear forecast gain beyond recent rainfall in a 2008-2025 Maritime Continent test
abstract: We tested whether current Nino 3.4 anomalies improve the next three months of mean rainfall over 10 S-10 N, 95 E-140 E. We used fixed GPCP V2.3 and CPC ERSSTv5 data. Models were fit on 237 origins in 1988-2007 and tested on 213 origins in 2008-2025. The baseline used calendar month and recent local rainfall, with season-specific slopes. Four added Nino terms raised test mean squared error by 9.4%. The 95% paired 36-month block interval for error reduction was -36.6% to +11.5%. Test RMSE rose from 0.7914 to 0.8278 mm/day. The Nino model had higher correlation but a larger dry mean error. A planned common time trend changed the point estimate to a 6.1% gain. Thus the primary test gives no clear added gain, and the conclusion depends on trend treatment. This is a retrospective test of revised products, not an operational forecast or a test of physical cause. The region includes land and ocean. The package gives code, monthly evidence, forecasts, block draws, source hashes, a figure, and independent numerical checks.

display.caption: Fixed test forecasts, yearly paired error changes, and planned checks. The primary bar shows a conditional 95% interval. Positive reductions favor the added Nino model.
